embodiment_note: Plugin architecture forbids Task delegation from sub-agents; chair embodied 10 TP lenses internally (strategist / devil's advocate / critical reviewer / ROI / risk engineer / domain expert / operator / security auditor / pragmatist / innovator). Vote derived from convergence across those lenses applied to previews.json + spot-checked mockup HTML.

top5.rationale: Strongest Gemma-4-feature exhibition: 4-function dispatch matrix, function_call_contract.yaml schema with line ranges, defer_to_human-first ordering, SystemPrompt.swift verbatim, Phase enum tied to configurable thinking — the 3 load-bearing Gemma 4 capabilities (function calling / 256K context / configurable thinking) are exhibited not asserted.

Highest engineering rigor: explicit Limitations section (L1 wondering-log Phase 4 stub, L2 single-machine n=10, L3 single-locked Korean tone) + numbered citations [1]–[14] + falsifiable claim framing — the only advocate that proactively concedes shipped-vs-designed-for boundary as a peer-reviewer-grade trust signal.

Best metric handling: charts render from actual firstChunkMs samples in claudedocs/bench/2026-05-06-latency-bench.json with p10/p50/p90 + n + hardware + uncertainty bounds; 24.0× speedup framed against slow-fallback first-chunk (correct comparator), not the marketing-baseline number. Inspection-ready by construction.

Most architecturally honest reframing: positions SocraticEngine as a Swift Package with the .app as one consumer of N. The NO-CLOUD invariant becomes a property the package guarantees to embedders, public API surface (EngineCoordinator / Phase / FunctionCallOrchestrator / TTSManager / AudioInputManager / TurnOutput / Mode / VisemeID) is enumerated correctly per CLAUDE.md stable-surface list.

Cleanest NO-CLOUD treatment: entitlements XML inline + inverted threat model with zero outbound arrows + 8-FAQ refutation of common 'but it must phone home' assumptions (telemetry / model updates / license check / crash reports / analytics / A/B tests / prompt logging / federated learning). Evidence-first, prose-second.

top3_final.rationale: P25 is the only advocate that satisfies the Gemma-feature criterion through exhibition rather than assertion. The dispatch matrix renders the 4 functions with their actual contract semantics (defer_to_human as guard, ask_back as the only generative path, surface_past_wonder against 256K context, mode_classify driving Phase enum), the configurable thinking mode is correctly mapped to Phase.thinking visualization, and the orchestration sequence reflects function_call_contract.yaml step ordering. Of all 26 advocates, this is the one a Gemma 4 evaluator would walk away citing as 'they used the model the way it was designed to be used' — load-bearing not decorative. Technical correctness on every Gemma 4 surface (function calling / 256K / thinking) is the highest bar this panel measures, and P25 clears it with the most material on-page.

P22 is the most defensible piece of technical writing in the set. The Abstract / Methods / Results / Discussion / Limitations / References scaffold treats every metric as a falsifiable claim with a numbered citation; the Limitations section explicitly draws the shipped-vs-designed-for line that the project's CLAUDE.md anti-pattern #6 demands. Crucially, P22 cites TTFT_median = 192 ms with n, hardware, and the bench file path — exactly the rigor a peer-reviewer-style judge needs to score Technical credibly. The paper-form reframing risks looking austere, but it is the framing least likely to embarrass the project under technical scrutiny, and the only one that makes the Phase 4 stub disclosure a feature of the trust contract rather than a footnote.

P13 wins the data-handling axis decisively: the TTFT distribution chart is drawn from the actual ten firstChunkMs samples in the bench JSON (not a stylized facsimile), p10/p50/p90 are computed correctly, and the 24.0× speedup is framed against the slow-fallback first-chunk comparator (which is the engineering-honest comparator) rather than the misleading 4.6 s baseline. Methodology table includes hardware/n/p10/p50/p90 — the four pieces of context any technical evaluator demands before trusting a latency number. Edges P19 for 3rd because raw bench-handling rigor speaks more directly to the technical-execution rubric than the SDK-reframing thesis, even though both are strong.

watch_list.concern: Deliberately substitutes 'engine' for 'model' and 'a bust that asks back' for 'LLM'. For the Impact-Education narrative this is defensible, but for the Technical lens it is self-sabotage: the Gemma-feature criterion explicitly rewards exhibiting the model's native capabilities (function calling, 256K context, configurable thinking) — and P26's lexicon hides exactly that surface. Spec-alignment claim that 'load-bearing technical content is unchanged' is partially undercut by the framing choice.

Pitch-deck cadence + 'try / star / share' ask bar borrows monetization-funnel vocabulary that does not match a non-monetized hackathon submission. Technical content is intact but the framing dilutes engineering signal — the Hook/Problem/Insight/Proof slide pattern de-prioritizes the dispatch matrix and bench methodology in favor of one-line summaries.

XP scroll meter + Evidence Badge HUD adds a UI layer on top of the evaluator's actual reading task. Spec_alignment_notes correctly insist tone stays severe and copy stays sourced, but the badge-unlock mechanic + viseme keyframe scroll-driving + dispatch console widget pull engineering attention away from the engineering content. Risk: a fatigued judge reads the form, not the evidence.

TCO ledger ($0/month × 9 line items) is a rhetorical frame, not engineering evidence. The 'cost story and privacy story are the same story' insight is sound but the 9-row ledger is contrived (auth / monitoring / CDN / TLS / backup / scaling have no architectural counterpart in this project). Acceptable for ROI lens, weak for technical lens.

Contributor avatars + role badges + branch policy + Conventional Commit scopes are org-process surfaces, not technical-execution surfaces. The artifact treats the project as a multi-author workspace but the Two-Weeks-Team structure is not the technical claim being evaluated. NO-CLOUD + abstention + PR-Λ all surface, but they share the page with workspace chrome that competes for the judge's attention.

The 'no ops surface' inversion is true but operates as an assertion rather than evidence. Without a status board grounded in actual artifacts (entitlements file, bench JSON, swift-testing scenarios), the page-as-status-board reads as a rhetorical move. P12 makes a stronger version of this argument with file-path-level evidence.

panel_summary: Technical Panel converges on P25 (Gemma 4 feature exhibition) > P22 (peer-reviewer rigor with explicit Limitations) > P13 (bench-derived charts with correct comparator) as the top-3 on engineering merit. P19 and P12 round out the top-5 with the strongest SDK-architecture and NO-CLOUD-evidence treatments respectively. Watch list flags six advocates whose framing choices either hide the engineering signal (P26 lexicon, P21 monetization cadence) or substitute organizational/cost rhetoric for technical evidence (P15, P04, P02), plus P23 whose HUD form competes with its sourced content. None of the watch-list six are technically wrong — they are technically muffled.
